hypothesis.physical_signature_targeted: Multi-scale curvature anomaly edges + thermal-gradient corridors representing hydrothermal alteration zones that lack surface fault expression in USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue.
hypothesis.why_catches_missing_faults: Standard registry patterns (dotted-ridge) replicate known H19-5 network segments. This hypothesis targets alteration zones adjacent to hidden fault tips that do not surface as lineaments, using curvature discontinuity rather than line replication.
hypothesis.difference_from_repo_implementations: Repo uses dotted-ridge replication (GEMSDOE25/GEMSDOE29 family), top-k emission (GEMSDOE30), or Poisson lattice (GEMSDOE32). This uses multi-scale curvature discontinuity detection with no point-pattern replication from H19-5.

mechanism: Compute curvature at 300m, 600m, 1200m from DEM; detect local maxima of curvature-gradient magnitude; weight by simulated thermal-proxy intensity; place confidence-weighted dots along anomaly edges; suppress any region within 500m of visible USGS catalogue faults to avoid duplication.
mimicking_non_fault_process: Erosional scarps, fluvial terraces, and glacial moraines can produce curvature discontinuities at similar scales. These are distinguished by: (a) alignment with regional stress direction, (b) correlation with thermal proxy, (c) exclusion of fluvially-aligned linear features via aspect-ratio filter.
